# Agent Skill Linter

**Headline:** A new `skill-linter` skill that scans `SKILL.md` and `AGENTS.md` files in the tracked skills tree, removes duplicated content and non-essential work-item IDs / workflow-comment noise, and produces a permission-gated recommendation report for content removal and brevity rewrites — scheduled to run at least weekly.

## Problem statement

The `skill/*/SKILL.md` and `AGENTS.md` files in this repository are the canonical source of the deployed agent skills (via the `~/.pi/agent/skills` symlink), and they have grown organically: content is duplicated across files, work-item IDs and workflow-traceability prose accumulate inline, and verbose blocks survive past their usefulness. The earlier one-off refactor (SA-0MRGTMMBB003H1QT) trimmed these files manually, but nothing keeps them from regressing. Agents load these files on every session, so bloat directly costs context budget and directive clarity.

## Users

- **AI agents** running Pi sessions — they load `SKILL.md` and `AGENTS.md` as instructions; lean, deduplicated files mean less context consumed and clearer directives.
- **Human maintainers** editing skills — a linter report with full context around proposed deletions makes review fast and safe.
- **Operators** running the weekly maintenance schedule — the report tells them exactly what to approve.

### Example user stories

- **As an** agent operator, **I want** a weekly skill-linter run, **so that** skills stay concise and deduplicated without manual effort.
- **As a** maintainer, **I want** proposed removals and rewrites presented with full context, **so that** I can approve or reject each change with confidence.
- **As an** agent, **I want** SKILL.md files free of non-essential work-item IDs and workflow comments, **so that** my context window is spent on instructions, not traceability noise.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deterministic duplicate detection:** The linter identifies duplicated content within and across the `skill/*/SKILL.md` files (and the repo `AGENTS.md` / `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`), reporting file paths, line spans, and the duplicated text for each instance.
- **AC2 — Automatic safe fixes:** Running with `--apply` removes exact-duplicate content and clearly non-essential work-item IDs / workflow-comment noise (heuristic rules documented in the skill reference); `--dry-run` (default for the scheduled run) reports exactly what would change with full context and changes nothing.
- **AC3 — Permission-gated recommendations:** Content that could be removed (but is not clearly safe) and content that could be rewritten for brevity without losing clarity are reported with full context (file, section, current text, proposed text, rationale) and are never modified automatically — applying them requires explicit operator approval.
- **AC4 — Weekly scheduling:** The skill ships a cron-install helper (e.g. `--install-cron weekly`) and documents the installed line; a weekly `--dry-run` report is produced on schedule.
- **AC5 — Test coverage and regression gate:** Unit tests cover duplicate detection, ID/comment stripping, and report formatting; a changed-scope test gate passes; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- **AC6 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full suite:** The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Skill authors can run one command to keep all skills and agent instructions lean and deduplicated, with every proposed change reviewable before it is applied — no more manual hygiene sweeps or regressing bloat.

## Constraints

- **Repo boundary:** the new skill lives in `skill/skill-linter/` (scripts, tests, SKILL.md) with a reference doc in `docs/dev/`; the context-budget gate (`docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`) must not be exceeded by the new files.
- **Read-only by default:** the linter must never modify files unless explicitly run with `--apply` (or an approved recommendation is applied by the operator); the weekly run is `--dry-run`.
- **No LLM dependency for core detection:** duplicate/ID detection must be deterministic (regex + structural comparison); LLM assistance is optional for brevity *recommendations* and must never gate the deterministic core.
- **Follow existing skill conventions:** hyphenated skill name, SKILL.md in the skill dir, scripts under `scripts/`, tests under `tests/`, shared-library imports resolved via the global skills path only (no script copies).
- **No scope creep:** this item creates the linter skill and its report/apply machinery; it does not itself rewrite the existing skill files (that is follow-up work driven by the first weekly report).

## Existing state

- `skill/*/SKILL.md` — 23+ files, ~6,000 lines total; known duplication and inline work-item IDs (e.g. audit 68, ship 26, test 17, report 12, implement 9 occurrences of `SA-…` IDs).
- `AGENTS.md` (repo root + `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` at repo root) — loaded as global agent instructions.
- One-off refactor epic **SA-0MRGTMMBB003H1QT** (completed) already trimmed these files once; no automated regression guard exists today.
- Related tooling exists: `context-audit` skill measures context size of these files (regression gate), and `ste100-experiment` measured STE-style brevity — neither lints content quality.

## Desired change

Introduce `skill/skill-linter/` with a CLI (`lint_skills.py`, style consistent with sibling skills): scan → detect duplicates / non-essential IDs & workflow comments / removable content / rewrite candidates → emit a structured report (text or JSON) with full context per finding → `--apply` applies only the safe-fix classes → `--install-cron weekly` prints/installs a crontab line for the weekly dry-run report. The skill is invoked as `/skill:skill-linter` with the same script-resolution pattern as sibling skills (`$(skill_path skill-linter)/scripts/...`).

## Key Files:

- `skill/skill-linter/SKILL.md` — new skill definition (lint rules, invocation, permission flow).
- `skill/skill-linter/scripts/lint_skills.py` — deterministic scanner + report generator + `--apply`/`--dry-run`/`--install-cron`/`--json` flags.
- `skill/skill-linter/tests/test_lint_skills.py` — unit tests for duplicate detection, ID stripping, report formatting, dry-run immutability.
- `docs/dev/skill-linter-reference.md` — reference doc: rules, heuristics, exit codes, cron installation.
- `skill/*/SKILL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — lint targets (read-only unless `--apply`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **False-positive deletions** — a heuristic could flag content as duplicated/non-essential when it is meaningful; mitigated by `--dry-run` as the default, full context in every report entry, and `--apply` only touching the clearly-safe fix classes.
- **LLM-variance in brevity recommendations** — LLM-produced rewrite proposals may vary run to run; mitigated by keeping them recommendation-only (never auto-applied) and requiring operator approval.
- **Cron not actually installed** — the helper prints the cron line for the operator to install (mirrors `wiki_watch`); the skill must not claim the schedule is active until installed.
- **Context-budget regression** — the new SKILL.md + scripts add context; must fit the existing `context-budget.thresholds.json` gate or the gate is updated deliberately (follow-up, not this item).
- **Assumption: repo is the lint target** — linting `skill/` + repo-root `AGENTS.md`/`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` covers the deployed skills because `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to this repo's `skill/`.
- **Assumption: skill does not rewrite existing files in this item** — the first weekly report drives follow-up work; this item only builds the linter (scope-creep guard).

## Related work

- **SA-0MRGTMMBB003H1QT** (completed) — one-off epic "Refactor AGENTS.md, commands, and skill files for conciseness and to remove duplication"; this linter is the automated, repeatable successor.
- **SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G** (completed) — "SorraAgents AGENTS.md: reference global instead of duplicating 20KB"; the AGENTS.md de-duplication precedent the linter should enforce (find-related report, 2026-11-14).
- **SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W** (completed) — split global vs project AGENTS.md (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` canonical source + symlink install); relevant to the linter's AGENT/AGENTS.md scope.
- **SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB** (completed) — "Refactor command/doc.md for conciseness"; sibling one-off conciseness refactor in the same spirit.
- **SA-0MSLK72KI006N9KP / SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1** (completed) — startup-context measurement and context-budget gate (`measure_context.py`, `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`); linter must not regress these gates.
- **`skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`** — measures the same files; complementary (measures size, linter improves quality).
- **`skill/ste100-experiment/`** — STE-style brevity experiment; relevant evidence for the brevity-recommendation rule design.
- **`skill/author-command/SKILL.md`** — skill-authoring conventions to follow.

> Related-work report also inserted into the item description by `find_related` (IDs SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB, SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W, SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: Which SKILL.md/AGENTS.md files should the linter examine? — Answer (operator, via "continue"): **Recommended option A accepted — SorraAgents repo only** (`skill/` + repo-root AGENTS.md); the repo IS the canonical source of deployed skills (`~/.pi/agent/skills` symlinks to it), so repo-only scope covers the deployment. CLI accepts a `--target` path so broader scans are possible later. Source: interactive reply ("continue").
- Q2: Lint only AGENT.md, only AGENTS.md, or both variants? — Answer (operator, via "continue"): **Recommended option C accepted — both variants treated identically.** Source: interactive reply ("continue").
- Q3: Output format? — Answer (operator, via "continue"): **Recommended option A + description text — report-only by default**, applying only the explicitly-authorized safe-fix classes under `--apply` (per item description: duplicated content and non-essential IDs/comments are removed; removals and brevity rewrites are recommended and require permission). Source: interactive reply ("continue") + canonical description wording.

## Objective

Add the read-only, unit-testable **bump preflight helper** used by the ship skill's new version-bump evaluation step. It gathers the release candidates and renders a compact review packet. It performs **no judgement and no mutation** — the agent judges, the producer approves.

## User Story

As the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`, I want a single helper that gathers every release candidate and renders the evidence I need to judge the release's importance, so that my patch/minor/major call is based on the items' content rather than guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- New module `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` exports a `gatherReleaseCandidates` (name may vary) that resolves candidates through an **injectable fetch boundary** (default `getCandidateItems()` from `check-audit-gate.js`); tests inject fakes and never read the live worklog.
- The helper enriches each candidate with the fields needed to judge importance: `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, the `## Impact` section or user story, and a truncated description excerpt. It tolerates missing fields (falls back to the title/id and an empty excerpt) without throwing.
- The helper renders a review packet (Markdown or plain text) that includes: the current version, the three candidate outcomes computed via the **existing** `bump-version.js` arithmetic (`bumpVersion`), and the per-item evidence listed above. It reuses `resolveVersionSource`/`bumpVersion` (no duplicated semver arithmetic).
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics (`bumpVersion`) rather than duplicating version arithmetic anywhere in the new helper.
- An **empty or unreadable candidate set** fails safe: the helper reports `patch` as the proposal, logs a warning explaining why, and never throws or blocks a release.
- Gathering/rendering is **purely read-only** — the helper performs no `git`, tag, PR, or `wl` mutation.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` covers: candidate gathering via the injected boundary, rendering of every packet field, the empty candidate set (patch + warning), and that `minor`/`major` outcomes reset the lower components correctly (delegated to `bumpVersion`).
- Tests pass via the test skill (`run_tests.py --scope changed`, node suite) and touch no live worklog or real git state.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the failing test file first (`test_bump_preflight.mjs`, `node:test`).
2. Add `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` with an exported preflight function accepting `{ getCandidateItemsFn, repoRoot }` injection.
3. Project `version` from the resolved version source; compute `patch`/`minor`/`major` outcomes with `bumpVersion`.
4. Render the packet with a stable, agent-readable layout; truncate description excerpts (e.g. ~200 chars).
5. Return a structured result (`{ candidates, currentVersion, proposals, proposedBump, warning }`) as well as the rendered text, so tests can assert fields directly.
6. Export a small render/format function so the workflow contract test can rely on a stable API.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` (new)
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (reuse `getCandidateItems`)
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` (reuse `resolveVersionSource`, `bumpVersion`)

## Constraints

- No issue-type or priority classifier — the helper only gathers/renders evidence.
- No mutation and no new git side effects.
- Empty/unreadable candidates default to `patch` with a warning.

## Deliverables

- `bump-preflight.js` with tests, passing the changed-scope suite.
